To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the floodplain soil bacterial community structure is more strongly affected by depth than by the landscape position, 2) the buried carbon‐rich soil horizon between 0 and 2 m depth is phylogenetically similar across the landscape, and 3) bacterial diversity in the deeper floodplain soils is as high if not even higher than in the upper soil layers.

(1) floodplain soils are characterized by high bacterial diversity, (2) soil depth is the main driver shaping the bacterial community structure, and (3) bacterial community structure is strongly affected by the soil organic carbon content.
